target_customer: Young adults in cities who pay to attend curated in-person events with strangers, plus venues that pay for foot traffic
problem: People struggle to meet new people offline; 222 matches strangers by an algorithm for real-life experiences without swiping, profiles or DMs.
business_model: Consumer marketplace: attendees pay to confirm a spot (early events cost $2.22) and partner venues pay for foot traffic

founders.name: Danial Hashemi
founders.background_notes: Described on YC as an Iranian immigrant building a new solution to social.

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching quiz, recommendations and a mobile app are standard engineering. The hard parts are operations: venue partnerships and event logistics.

defensibility.rationale: Venue relationships and city density help, but dinner and event matching services copy easily and earlier social dining startups such as Grubwithus existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced incumbent action found. Meetup and Bumble BFF were not confirmed in sources and are listed as plausible only.

market_need_then: Press framed the product as an anti-metaverse real life social app for Gen Z (dot.LA), with loneliness cited later by Fast Company in 2025.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful serendipity: No Swiping, No Profiles, No DMs.

branding.brand_signature: No swiping, no profiles, no DMs and the $2.22 event price tied to the name
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch (Oct 2023), Los Angeles Times (Oct 2023), Business Insider (Feb 2024), Fast Company (Jun 2025) and WSJ (Dec 2025) per its YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive numeric name and repeated national press, with the $2.22 price echoing the name, but no merch or user community evidence sourced.

outcome_analysis: 222 started as a three person Los Angeles events operation in 2022, launched an app in February 2024 and expanded to New York, San Francisco and Chicago. Aggregators report a Series A near $10M in December 2025 and a much larger team, which suggests traction, but funding is unverified in primary sources.
notes: Unverified funding from aggregators only: Series A about $10.1M on 2025-12-23 led by Upfront Ventures with General Catalyst (one source), an earlier seed near $2.5M in 2024-02, totals quoted from $11.6M to $14.0M, other listed investors 1517 Fund, Best Nights VC and Scrum Ventures. None recorded as rounds. Fast Company article returned 403 and was not read. Founded year conflicts (2022 per LA move in early 2022, 2023 per YC page). Competitors: no dated sources near the batch list competitors; only 2011 to 2013 social dining startups (Grubwithus, GrubTonight) surfaced, which are not near the batch. Employee counts conflict (28 on YC, 185 on Dealroom).
